task.title: Finalize local Ollama/OpenCode autonomous factory
task.diagnostic: Le runner local est l'architecture cible. Le cloud workflow ne doit pas devenir une seconde implementation loop. Valider et durcir le chemin local PC allumé -> Ollama -> OpenCode -> queue AUTOPILOT -> tests -> PR.
evidence: Repository already contains local factory runner and shared .ai contracts.
Founder requires zero external LLM API keys and no concurrent cloud implementation loop.
implementation: Treat local Ollama/OpenCode as the sole implementation runner.
Ensure startup/recovery is deterministic when Windows boots and the runner is restarted.
Ensure the runner can consume AUTOPILOT issues without manual prompt copy/paste.
Ensure Ollama is detected locally and failure is explicit/recoverable.
Prevent the cloud workflow from creating a competing implementation loop; disable/remove it if it conflicts with the local architecture.
Keep GitHub Actions for CI/CD and verification only where appropriate.
Do not add Anthropic/OpenAI credentials or external LLM dependencies.
tests: Run a deterministic dry-run/local-agent availability check.
Verify an AUTOPILOT issue can enter the local queue without manual copy/paste.
acceptance: PC on + local runner started once is sufficient for continuous autonomous cycles.
No Anthropic/OpenAI API key is required.
No second cloud implementation agent can compete with the local runner.
A queued AUTOPILOT task is automatically consumed by the local runner.
Failures park/retry cleanly instead of deadlocking.
task.metric: zero manual prompt handoffs; zero concurrent implementation runners
task.rollback: Revert only the factory orchestration changes; preserve product code.
constraints: Do not delete the local factory.
Do not introduce a paid external LLM dependency.
task.stopCondition: Stop if Ollama is unavailable, credentials are unexpectedly required, or existing factory tests fail; report the blocker instead of bypassing it.

task.title: Connect local watchdog, AUTOPILOT issue bridge, CI status and ChatGPT reporting
task.diagnostic: The founder wants the already-installed Windows local agent to keep working while the PC is on, consume GitHub missions without prompt copy/paste, report real progress to GitHub, and let ChatGPT monitor/communicate through the same durable channel. A GitHub issue exists for local factory hardening (#794); do not duplicate or restart the runner.
implementation: Inspect the live bridge contract, issue poller, queue importer, lock format and status reporter before changing anything. Reuse the existing runner and single-instance lock.
Verify the exact GitHub source the local bridge polls (issue body, comments, labels, or a workflow). Document the contract and make one supported path reliable.
Make issue ingestion idempotent using a durable task ID/correlation ID; duplicate polling or comments must not start duplicate jobs.

Make the local runner acknowledge a received task on the same GitHub issue, report started/heartbeat/blocked/completed states, and include branch, commit SHA, test result and artifact links when available.

Implement or repair a bounded Windows watchdog using the existing Factory-Control-Runner / scheduled task installation where present. It must check process health, respect the existing bridge lock, avoid concurrent starts, throttle restarts and log recoverable failures. Do not create a second competing runner.

Keep GitHub Actions as CI/verification and status reporting, not as a second code-writing implementation loop. Correlate CI results to the exact task ID and commit SHA; the local runner must be able to observe the result through GitHub.

Document the ChatGPT-to-GitHub handoff: ChatGPT can post task/status messages through GitHub; the local runner only receives them automatically if its verified polling contract watches that channel. Never claim direct Windows access from a ChatGPT scheduled task.
Add deterministic tests for duplicate delivery, issue acknowledgement, lock contention, watchdog restart limits, CI status correlation and clean recovery.
Use existing free/local models when available. Do not introduce paid APIs or new credentials.
acceptance: One existing local runner only; lock remains authoritative.
A new AUTOPILOT issue is automatically consumed without manual prompt copy/paste when the PC and bridge are running.
The same issue receives real status and exact task/commit/check correlation.
A stopped runner can be recovered by the existing or repaired Windows watchdog without duplicate execution.
CI status is traceable to the commit and can be reported back without a cloud implementation loop.
Documented dry-run proves issue -> local queue -> acknowledgement -> branch/commit -> CI result -> final status; all steps share a correlation ID.
No merge or production deploy is triggered. Existing Sargagame delivery policy remains enforced.
constraints: No production merge/deploy or bypass of sargagame.enabled=false.
No payments, pricing, checkout, webhooks, grants, Supabase schema or secrets changes.
Do not print or commit secrets, tokens, cookies or environment files.
Do not start a competing runner or terminate the existing runner as a first step.
Do not claim that Windows has been changed unless the local runner produces evidence.
If local access is not available, implement/test the safe GitHub-side portion and report precisely what requires the PC.
tests: Dry-run issue ingestion with a unique task ID.
Single-runner lock contention and recovery test.
CI result correlated to exact commit SHA.
Watchdog restart policy / no duplicate process test.
task.metric: zero manual prompt handoffs; zero duplicate runs; complete task-to-CI correlation
task.rollback: Revert orchestration-only changes; preserve product code and the existing runner.
